shifts.summary: The paper was reported as easy to moderate overall. Reasoning was moderate with at least eight analytical questions. Quantitative section was described as moderate to difficult, with timing pressure and many varied topics. General awareness and English were both moderate in difficulty.

sections.name: General Intelligence & Reasoning
sections.notes: At least 8 analytical questions; reasoning was doable.

sections.name: Quantitative Aptitude
sections.notes: Sectional timing: 15 min for 25 Q, causing trouble. Various tricks and shortcuts were discussed for each problem.

topics.topic: Ratio of percentages (a% of b vs b% of a)
Profit sharing investment problem (Alok and Deep)
Area ratio of triangle ADE to quadrilateral DECB
Average age problem with teacher added

asked.q: Which address is different among the three address‑based questions?
Find x to make 7,9,8,11 proportional after subtraction.
Length of internal common tangent for circles radius 9 cm and 5 cm, centers 17 cm apart.
If a = 15% of b and b = 25% of a, find the ratio a:b.
Profit sharing ratio between Alok (starts ₹0) and Deep (starts ₹1200) with given investments.
Ratio of area of triangle ADE to quadrilateral DECB in triangle ABC with line through centroid parallel to BC.
Teacher joins 19 students with avg age 17, new avg 18; find teacher's age.
Sphere volume 36π, cylinder with same radius and height 2r; find remaining volume.
Average salary of 80 employees is ₹20,000; 30 earn ₹72,000 avg; find avg of remaining 50.
Two hemispheres radius 6 cm and 8 cm melt to form new hemisphere; approximate new radius.
In triangle, angle bisector at incenter, angle B C =125°, find angle B A C.

observations: Quant section timing was tight, 15 minutes for 25 questions.
Many quantitative problems required shortcuts and tricks.
Reasoning included a notable number of analytical address questions.
General awareness had only one current‑affairs item reported.
disagreements: One report called Quant difficult, another called it moderate.

intro: The partial analysis for Shift 1 of the SSC CGL 2026 Tier 1 exam held on 27 October 2026 describes the paper as overall easy to moderate. Reasoning questions were moderate with at least eight analytical items, while the quantitative section was seen as moderate to difficult with timing pressure. General awareness and English sections were also moderate in difficulty. The reported figure of 20–21 candidates achieving good attempts is unofficial, and SSC normally normalises scores across shifts. No usable analysis has been published yet for Shifts 2 and 3, pending further candidate evidence.

faqs.q: What overall difficulty was reported for the SSC CGL 2026 Tier 1 exam on 27 October 2026?
faqs.a: The partial review for Shift 1 indicates the paper was overall easy to moderate; the other shifts have no published analysis yet.

faqs.q: How many candidates were reported to have good attempts on 27 October 2026?
faqs.a: The partial analysis mentions an unofficial estimate of 20–21 candidates with good attempts for Shift 1; this figure is not official.

faqs.q: Which sections were described as moderate or difficult on 27 October 2026?
faqs.a: Reasoning was moderate with at least eight analytical questions; quantitative was moderate to difficult with timing pressure; General awareness and English were both moderate.

faqs.q: Why is there no analysis for Shifts 2 and 3 on 27 October 2026?
faqs.a: Both shifts are marked as pending because sufficient candidate evidence has not yet been collected to produce a usable review.

faqs.q: Does SSC provide official difficulty ratings for the 27 October 2026 exam?
faqs.a: SSC does not release official difficulty ratings; the available assessments are based on candidate feedback and are unofficial, with scores normalised across shifts.
